evidence.why: Configures one indexed set using a boundary and complementary flags.

facts.rationale: Distinguishes the indexed single-set partition configurator from the fighter-wide flag dispatcher and resolves the observed rendered collision. Does not assign an unsupported animation-tree meaning to the split argument.

evidence.why: Explicit boolean is forwarded to the solver; wrapper supplies x2228_b1.

facts.rationale: Distinguishes the two-argument implementation from the public one-argument wrapper while preserving uncertainty about the boolean's precise semantic name.

evidence.why: Table lookup and separate x590 restoration flow.
Table argument is cast to boundary/token values.
Actual FigaTree, frame and speed consumer.

facts.rationale: Separates the numerically consumed table entries from the actual ordinary-animation tree and preserves all input and output paths.
facts.value: Snapshots cur_anim_frame and frame_speed_mul. With x594_b4 set, indexes ft_data->x2C->x10 using x28[anim_id][1]; if the selected array is non-null, passes each pointer-typed table value to ftCo_8009CB40 in mode 1. That callee interprets the value as an integer chain boundary/token, not as a dereferenced FigaTree. Otherwise, when x594_b3 is set, passes mode 0 and NULL. In either processed loop, non-null x590 is separately supplied to ftAnim_8006EED4 with the authored starting bone, saved frame and speed.

facts.rationale: Corrects unsupported tree-binding interpretation without discarding the supported dynamics/animation handoff.
facts.value: Coordinates fighter dynamic-bone participation with ordinary skeletal animation by applying animation-selected chain partitions or the mode-0 configuration, then optionally restoring the active fighter animation on affected part subtrees. The dynamics table is pointer-typed in this revision, but its entries are consumed numerically; this path does not establish that secondary-motion animation trees are installed.

facts.rationale: Describes the demonstrated operation rather than claiming each set receives an installed FigaTree or is uniformly enabled.
facts.value: Applies the fighter's animation-dependent dynamic-chain flag configuration to existing sets and optionally restores ordinary animation at the saved frame and speed on each processed set's authored root. The prioritized x594_b4 path supplies per-set numeric split tokens from a pointer-typed table; the x594_b3 path supplies mode 0 with a null boundary.

facts.rationale: Preserves branch priority, null behavior and partial-chain semantics instead of equating mode 1 with uniform enablement.
facts.value: x594_b4 takes priority over x594_b3. Its outer x10 table is indexed without a null guard; a null selected array produces no changes and does not fall back to x594_b3. A non-null selected array causes mode-1 configuration of every runtime set using its table value as the split boundary, so nodes before that boundary are unflagged and remaining nodes are flagged. If x594_b4 is clear and x594_b3 is set, every runtime set receives mode 0 with NULL. Each processed set additionally restores ordinary animation only when x590 is non-null. Neither flag set produces no changes.

evidence.why: Exact equality tests and downstream calls.

facts.rationale: Corrects sign-wide language: exact onset +1 differs from positive continuing status 2, which E7B4 does accept through its >0 test.
facts.value: For MARS or EMBLEM with x2227_b6 clear, reads lb_80011ABC(). Exactly -1 delegates to ftCo_8009E4A8 and returns. Exactly +1, with x594_b4 or x594_b3 set, iterates the authored ft_data->x2C->dynamicsNum and calls ftCo_8009CB40(fp, i, 1, NULL). If x590 is non-null, passes the saved current frame and playback multiplier to ftAnim_8006EBE8 with zero blend duration, then calls ftAnim_8006E9B4. Other values, including continuing-wind value 2, do nothing here. The shared producer derives values 1, 2, -1 and 0 from directional-source aggregate strength and prior status.

evidence.why: One submission, duration default and constant return.
Position is copied; insertion result is discarded.

facts.rationale: Corrects guaranteed creation and preserves shared-pool failure/replacement branches and the source's independent lifetime.
facts.value: Per invocation, submits one point-wind request and always returns false, regardless of acceptance. Negative duration becomes 120; zero and positive values are forwarded. The library copies the transformed world-position snapshot and parameters into a free source slot, may replace an existing source according to its numeric priority rule, or may reject the request; this helper receives no success result. Accepted sources lose magnitude by the decay amount with a zero clamp, advance their phase counter, decrement positive duration and are recycled when duration is zero. They do not retain the Fighter joint as a moving attachment.

evidence.why: Motion entry supplies flags and metadata.

facts.rationale: Retains the motion-entry mapping while correcting an interpretation contradicted by the actual consumer of the table values.
facts.value: Implements motion-dependent selection of fighter dynamic-chain flags and participation boundaries. Motion entry supplies current animation flags and two-byte metadata; its second byte can select a per-set table whose pointer-typed entries are interpreted numerically by the chain configurator. This is configuration of existing dynamics, not demonstrated binding of secondary-motion FigaTrees.

evidence.why: Complete branch structure and character exceptions.

facts.rationale: Makes the exceptional all-kinds x594_b4 branch explicit and preserves the >0 status test, which includes continuing value 2.
facts.value: With anim_id != -1, x2227_b6 selects mode 0 through ordinary character dispatch. Otherwise MARS/EMBLEM with lb_80011ABC() > 0 select mode 1 through that dispatch. The remaining x594_b4 branch reads arg1[0][1], processes every runtime set without Kirby/Purin exclusions, and uses mode 0 with NULL if either x10 or its selected array is null; otherwise it uses mode 1 with each pointer-typed split token. Without x594_b4, x594_b3 selects ordinary mode 0 and its absence selects ordinary mode 1. Ordinary dispatch skips Kirby, handles only set 0 for Purin, and iterates all runtime sets for other kinds. With anim_id == -1, only x2227_b6 triggers ordinary mode-0 dispatch; otherwise nothing is changed.

evidence.why: Node recycling and allocation exhaustion behavior.
Character cleanup and descriptor release are separately ordered.

facts.rationale: Corrects universal full-range initialization and records useful ownership and exceptional-lifetime behavior supported across the TU and library.
facts.value: Maintains a capacity-checked runtime-set count and descriptor array on each Fighter. General character and Kirby-hat setup replace the count and initialize its indexed range; Purin costume setup is exceptional, acting only for costume IDs 2/3, setting count three and initializing slots 1/2 while preserving slot zero. These setup paths do not first release old sets or implement rollback for downstream node-pool exhaustion. Unloading releases every counted descriptor and clears the count; the library recycles nodes without destroying their associated JObjs. Model/accessory teardown and descriptor teardown therefore remain separate lifecycle operations.
